# Negativity (entanglement measure)
function negativity(ρ, dim_A, dim_B)
    """Compute negativity via partial transpose"""
    # Partial transpose (transpose subsystem B)
    ρ_TB = zeros(ComplexF64, dim_A*dim_B, dim_A*dim_B)
    
    for i in 1:dim_A
        for j in 1:dim_A
            for k in 1:dim_B
                for l in 1:dim_B
                    idx1 = (i-1)*dim_B + k
                    idx2 = (j-1)*dim_B + l
                    idx_TB1 = (i-1)*dim_B + l
                    idx_TB2 = (j-1)*dim_B + k
                    ρ_TB[idx_TB1, idx_TB2] = ρ[idx1, idx2]
                end
            end
        end
    end
    
    # Negativity = (||ρ^TB||₁ - 1) / 2
    eigenvals = eigvals(Hermitian(ρ_TB))
    trace_norm = sum(abs.(eigenvals))
    
    return (trace_norm - 1) / 2
end

# Concurrence (for 2-qubit states)
function concurrence(ρ)
    """Compute concurrence for 2-qubit state"""
    σ_y = [0 -im; im 0]
    σ_y_tensor = kron(σ_y, σ_y)
    
    ρ_tilde = σ_y_tensor * conj(ρ) * σ_y_tensor
    R = sqrt(sqrt(ρ) * ρ_tilde * sqrt(ρ))
    
    λ = sort(real(eigvals(R)), rev=true)
    
    C = max(0, λ[1] - λ[2] - λ[3] - λ[4])
    return C
end

# ============================================================
# FACTORIAL DESIGN OF EXPERIMENTS
# ============================================================

struct FactorialDesign
    factors::Vector{Symbol}
    levels::Dict{Symbol, Vector{Float64}}
    design_matrix::Matrix{Float64}
    responses::Vector{Float64}
end

function create_factorial_design(factors::Vector{Symbol}, levels::Dict{Symbol, Vector{Float64}})
    """Create full factorial design."""
    
    n_factors = length(factors)
    n_levels_per_factor = [length(levels[f]) for f in factors]
    n_runs = prod(n_levels_per_factor)
    
    design_matrix = zeros(n_runs, n_factors)
    
    # Generate factorial combinations
    run = 1
    indices = ones(Int, n_factors)
    
    while run <= n_runs
        for (i, factor) in enumerate(factors)
            design_matrix[run, i] = levels[factor][indices[i]]
        end
        
        # Increment indices
        indices[1] += 1
        for i in 1:(n_factors-1)
            if indices[i] > n_levels_per_factor[i]
                indices[i] = 1
                indices[i+1] += 1
            end
        end
        
        run += 1
    end
    
    # Placeholder responses (would be measured)
    responses = zeros(n_runs)
    
    return FactorialDesign(factors, levels, design_matrix, responses)
end

function evaluate_design!(design::FactorialDesign, objective_function::Function)
    """Evaluate design points using objective function."""
    
    for i in 1:size(design.design_matrix, 1)
        x = design.design_matrix[i, :]
        design.responses[i] = objective_function(x)
    end
end

function fit_regression_model(design::FactorialDesign)
    """Fit linear regression model to factorial design."""
    
    X = design.design_matrix
    y = design.responses
    
    # Add intercept column
    X_aug = hcat(ones(size(X, 1)), X)
    
    # Ordinary least squares: β = (X'X)^(-1) X'y
    β = (X_aug' * X_aug) \ (X_aug' * y)
    
    # Compute R²
    y_pred = X_aug * β
    ss_res = sum((y .- y_pred).^2)
    ss_tot = sum((y .- mean(y)).^2)
    r_squared = 1 - ss_res / ss_tot
    
    return β, r_squared
end

# ============================================================
# RESPONSE SURFACE METHODOLOGY (RSM)
# ============================================================

struct ResponseSurface
    center::Vector{Float64}
    axial_distance::Float64
    design_points::Matrix{Float64}
    responses::Vector{Float64}
end

function create_central_composite_design(n_factors::Int; center=[0.0 for _ in 1:n_factors], α=√n_factors)
    """Create Central Composite Design for RSM."""
    
    # Factorial points (2^k)
    n_factorial = 2^n_factors
    factorial_points = zeros(n_factorial, n_factors)
    
    for i in 1:n_factorial
        for j in 1:n_factors
            factorial_points[i, j] = ((i-1) >> (j-1)) & 1 == 0 ? -1.0 : 1.0
        end
    end
    
    # Axial points (2k)
    axial_points = zeros(2 * n_factors, n_factors)
    for i in 1:n_factors
        axial_points[2*i-1, i] = α
        axial_points[2*i, i] = -α
    end
    
    # Center points
    center_point = zeros(1, n_factors)
    
    # Combine all points
    design_points = vcat(factorial_points, axial_points, center_point)
    
    # Translate to actual center
    for i in 1:size(design_points, 1)
        design_points[i, :] .+= center
    end
    
    responses = zeros(size(design_points, 1))
    
    return ResponseSurface(center, α, design_points, responses)
end

function fit_quadratic_model(rsm::ResponseSurface)
    """Fit quadratic response surface model."""
    
    X = rsm.design_points
    y = rsm.responses
    
    n, k = size(X)
    
    # Build design matrix for quadratic model
    # [1, x₁, x₂, ..., x₁², x₂², ..., x₁x₂, ...]
    n_terms = 1 + k + k + binomial(k, 2)
    X_quad = zeros(n, n_terms)
    
    col = 1
    
    # Intercept
    X_quad[:, col] .= 1
    col += 1
    
    # Linear terms
    for i in 1:k
        X_quad[:, col] = X[:, i]
        col += 1
    end
    
    # Quadratic terms
    for i in 1:k
        X_quad[:, col] = X[:, i].^2
        col += 1
    end
    
    # Interaction terms
    for i in 1:k
        for j in (i+1):k
            X_quad[:, col] = X[:, i] .* X[:, j]
            col += 1
        end
    end
    
    # Fit model
    β = (X_quad' * X_quad) \ (X_quad' * y)
    
    return β
end

"""

"""
struct HilbertSpaceOperator
    matrix::Matrix{ComplexF64}
    
    function HilbertSpaceOperator(M::Matrix)
        @assert size(M, 1) == size(M, 2) "El operador debe actuar en un espacio cuadrado."

    end

"""

"""
function spectral_radius(op::HilbertSpaceOperator)
    vals = eigvals(op.matrix)

end

"""
function operator_norm(op::HilbertSpaceOperator)
    return opnorm(op.matrix, 2)
end

println("\n💰 ESCENARIO:")

# Datos del problema
n_assets = 5
budget = 100_000.0

# Retornos esperados (% anual)
expected_returns = [0.12, 0.10, 0.08, 0.15, 0.09]  # 12%, 10%, 8%, 15%, 9%

# Matriz de covarianza (riesgo)
# Valores simplificados para demostración
Σ = [
    0.04  0.01  0.00  0.02  0.01;
    0.01  0.03  0.00  0.01  0.00;
    0.00  0.00  0.02  0.00  0.00;
    0.02  0.01  0.00  0.05  0.01;
    0.01  0.00  0.00  0.01  0.02
]

# Umbral de riesgo
risk_threshold = 0.03

println("   Presupuesto: \$$budget")
println("   Retornos esperados: ", expected_returns)
println("   Umbral de riesgo: $risk_threshold")

# MODELO DE OPTIMIZACIÓN CONVEXA
# ========================================

println("\n🔬 CONSTRUYENDO MODELO CONVEXO:")

# Variable de decisión: proporción invertida en cada activo
x = Variable(n_assets)

# Función objetivo: Maximizar retorno esperado
# (Equivalente a minimizar el negativo)
objective = maximize(dot(expected_returns, x))

# Restricciones
constraints = [
    sum(x) == 1,           # Invertir todo el presupuesto (100%)
    x >= 0,                # No posiciones cortas
    quadform(x, Σ) <= risk_threshold  # Riesgo ≤ umbral (CONVEXA!)
]

# RESOLVER
# ========================================

println("\n⚡ RESOLVIENDO...")

# Crear problema
problem = minimize(-objective.head, constraints)  # Minimizar negativo = maximizar

# Resolver
solve!(problem, ECOS.Optimizer; silent_solver=true)

# Verificar solución
if problem.status == MOI.OPTIMAL
    println("   ✅ Solución óptima encontrada (GLOBAL)")
    
    # Extraer resultados

using DynamicalSystems
using LinearAlgebra
using Plots

# 1. Definir el Sistema Caótico (Mapa de Hénon)
# x_{n+1} = 1 - a*x_n^2 + y_n
# y_{n+1} = b*x_n
@inline @inbounds function henon_rule(u, p, n)
    a, b = p
    x, y = u
    dx = 1.0 - a*x^2 + y
    dy = b*x
    return SVector(dx, dy)
end

# Parámetros caóticos clásicos

using Statistics

function analyze_capability(data::Vector{Float64}, lsl::Float64, usl::Float64)
    # 1. Estadísticos Básicos
    mu = mean(data)
    sigma_overall = std(data)
    
    # 2. Sigma Within (Método Moving Range / d2)
    mr = abs.(diff(data))
    mr_bar = mean(mr)
    d2 = 1.128
    sigma_within = mr_bar / d2
    
    # 3. Índices de Capacidad
    Cp = (usl - lsl) / (6 * sigma_within)
    Pp = (usl - lsl) / (6 * sigma_overall)
    
    Cpu = (usl - mu) / (3 * sigma_within)
    Cpl = (mu - lsl) / (3 * sigma_within)
    Cpk = min(Cpu, Cpl)
    
    Ppu = (usl - mu) / (3 * sigma_overall)
    Ppl = (mu - lsl) / (3 * sigma_overall)
    Ppk = min(Ppu, Ppl)
    
    # 4. Reporte
    println("\n" * "="^50)
    println("📊 PROCESS CAPABILITY ANALYSIS (Julia Engine)")
    println("="^50)
    println("N: $(length(data))")
    println("Mean: $(round(mu, digits=4))")
    println("Sigma (Within):  $(round(sigma_within, digits=4))")
    println("Sigma (Overall): $(round(sigma_overall, digits=4))")
    println("-"^50)
    println("LSL: $lsl  |  USL: $usl")
    println("-"^50)
    println("Cp:  $(round(Cp, digits=3))   Pp:  $(round(Pp, digits=3))")
    println("Cpk: $(round(Cpk, digits=3))  Ppk: $(round(Ppk, digits=3))")
    println("="^50)

# 📉 JARVIX SIX SIGMA: MEASUREMENT SYSTEM ANALYSIS (MSA)
# ========================================================
# Language: Pure Julia (Technical Excellence Standard)
# Method: Gage R&R (ANOVA Method)

using Statistics

struct GageResult
    ev::Float64    # Equipment Variation (Repeatability)
    av::Float64    # Appraiser Variation (Reproducibility)
    grr::Float64   # Gage R&R
    pv::Float64    # Part-to-Part Variation
    tv::Float64    # Total Variation
    ndc::Int       # Number of Distinct Categories
end

"""
    analyze_gage_rr(data, n_parts, n_appraisers, n_trials)

Calculates the Gage R&R components using the ANOVA-like approach.
Input: flattened array of measurements ordered by Trial, Appraiser, Part.
"""
function analyze_gage_rr(data::Vector{Float64}, n_parts::Int, n_appraisers::Int, n_trials::Int)
    # Reshape: [Part, Appraiser, Trial]
    reshaped_data = reshape(data, (n_parts, n_appraisers, n_trials))
    
    # 1. Means calculations
    grand_mean = mean(data)
    part_means = [mean(reshaped_data[i, :, :]) for i in 1:n_parts]
    appraiser_means = [mean(reshaped_data[:, j, :]) for j in 1:n_appraisers]
    
    # Range of averages
    Rp = maximum(part_means) - minimum(part_means)
    Ra = maximum(appraiser_means) - minimum(appraiser_means)
    
    # Average Range (R-bar)
    ranges = [maximum(reshaped_data[i, j, :]) - minimum(reshaped_data[i, j, :]) 
              for i in 1:n_parts, j in 1:n_appraisers]
    R_double_bar = mean(ranges)
    
    # 2. Constants (for standard samples, approximate)
    d2_repeat = 1.693  # For 2 trials
    d2_repro = 1.912   # For 3 appraisers
    
    # 3. Component Estimation
    EV = (R_double_bar / d2_repeat) # Repeatability
    AV_raw = (Ra / d2_repro)
    AV = sqrt(max(0, AV_raw^2 - (EV^2 / (n_parts * n_trials)))) # Reproducibility
    
    GRR = sqrt(EV^2 + AV^2) # Total Gage R&R
    PV = (Rp / 2.08) # Part Variation (approx d2 for parts)
    
    TV = sqrt(GRR^2 + PV^2) # Total Variation
    
    # Number of Distinct Categories
    ndc = Int(floor(1.41 * (PV / GRR)))
    
    return GageResult(EV, AV, GRR, PV, TV, ndc)
end

function print_executive_report(res::GageResult)
    println("\n" * "═"^60)
    println("📊 MSA EXECUTIVE REPORT - GAGE R&R (JULIA CORE)")
    println("═"^60)
    
    p_grr = (res.grr / res.tv) * 100
    p_ev  = (res.ev / res.tv) * 100
    p_av  = (res.av / res.tv) * 100
    p_pv  = (res.pv / res.tv) * 100
    
    println("Component            | % Contribution | Status")
    println("-"^60)
    
    status_grr = p_grr < 10 ? "✅ ACCEPTABLE" : (p_grr <= 30 ? "⚠️ MARGINAL" : "❌ UNACCEPTABLE")
    
    @printf("%-20s | %13.2f%% | %s\n", "Gage R&R (Total)", p_grr, status_grr)
    @printf("%-20s | %13.2f%% |\n", " - Repeatability", p_ev)
    @printf("%-20s | %13.2f%% |\n", " - Reproducibility", p_av)
    @printf("%-20s | %13.2f%% |\n", "Part-to-Part", p_pv)
    println("-"^60)
    println("Number of Distinct Categories (NDC): $(res.ndc)")
    
    if res.ndc >= 5
        println("NDC Status: ✅ PASS (>= 5)")
    else
        println("NDC Status: ❌ FAIL (< 5)")
    end
    println("═"^60 * "\n")
end

function qft(n::Int)
    n == 1 && return chain(1, put(1 => H))

using Statistics

"""
    simulate_ergodic_system(f, x0, n)

Simulates a dynamical system x_{n+1} = f(x_n) and calculates the time average
compared to the space average (assuming invariant measure).
"""
function simulate_ergodic_system(f::Function, x0::Float64, n::Int)
    trajectory = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    trajectory[1] = x0
    
    for i in 2:n
        trajectory[i] = f(trajectory[i-1])
    end
    
    time_averages = cumsum(trajectory) ./ (1:n)
    return trajectory, time_averages
end

using DifferentialEquations
using Statistics

export lorenz!, vanderpol!, driven_pendulum!, solve_system

"""
Lorenz System (Chaotic Attractor)
"""
function lorenz!(du, u, p, t)
    σ, ρ, β = p
    du[1] = σ * (u[2] - u[1])
    du[2] = u[1] * (ρ - u[3]) - u[2]
    du[3] = u[1] * u[2] - β * u[3]
end

"""
Van der Pol Oscillator (Limit Cycle)
"""
function vanderpol!(du, u, p, t)
    μ = p[1]
    du[1] = u[2]
    du[2] = μ * (1 - u[1]^2) * u[2] - u[1]
end

"""
Driven Damped Pendulum (Chaos in mechanics)
"""
function driven_pendulum!(du, u, p, t)
    # u = [θ, ω]
    # p = [q (damping), g (gravity), L (length), F (drive), Ω (freq)]
    q, g, L, F, Ω = p
    du[1] = u[2]
    du[2] = - (g/L)*sin(u[1]) - q*u[2] + F*cos(Ω*t)
end

function solve_system(prob_func, u0, tspan, p)
    prob = ODEProblem(prob_func, u0, tspan, p)
    return solve(prob, Tsit5(), reltol=1e-8, abstol=1e-8)
end

module MarkovAnalyzer

using Distributions
using LinearAlgebra
using Statistics

export MarkovChain, simulate, stationary_distribution, metropolis_hastings, gibbs_sampler

"""
    MarkovChain(P, states)

Representa una cadena de Markov de tiempo discreto.
Valida que P sea una matriz estocástica.
"""
struct MarkovChain
    P::Matrix{Float64}
    states::Vector{String}
    
    function MarkovChain(P::Matrix{Float64}, states::Vector{String})
        n = size(P, 1)
        @assert n == size(P, 2) "La matriz de transición debe ser cuadrada."
        @assert length(states) == n "El número de estados debe coincidir con la dimensión de P."
        @assert all(sum(P, dims=2) .≈ 1.0) "Cada fila de P debe sumar 1.0."
        @assert all(P .>= 0) "Las probabilidades no pueden ser negativas."
        new(P, states)
    end
end

"""
Simula la cadena de Markov por `n_steps` desde un estado inicial.
"""
function simulate(mc::MarkovChain, initial_state::Int, n_steps::Int)
    trajectory = zeros(Int, n_steps + 1)
    trajectory[1] = initial_state
    
    for t in 1:n_steps
        current = trajectory[t]
        trajectory[t+1] = rand(Categorical(mc.P[current, :]))
    end
    
    return trajectory
end

"""
Calcula la distribución estacionaria mediante autovectores.
"""
function stationary_distribution(mc::MarkovChain)
    # P' * pi = pi (encontrar autovector para lambda=1)
    vals, vecs = eigen(copy(mc.P'))
    idx = argmin(abs.(vals .- 1.0))
    π_vec = real(vecs[:, idx])
    return π_vec ./ sum(π_vec)
end

"""
MCMC: Algoritmo de Metropolis-Hastings para distribuciones arbitrarias.
"""
function metropolis_hastings(logp::Function, x0::Float64, n_samples::Int; σ=0.5)
    samples = zeros(n_samples)
    samples[1] = x0
    acc = 0
    
    for i in 2:n_samples
        x_prev = samples[i-1]
        x_prop = x_prev + randn() * σ
        
        # Ratio de aceptación
        log_α = logp(x_prop) - logp(x_prev)
        
        if log(rand()) < log_α
            samples[i] = x_prop
            acc += 1
        else
            samples[i] = x_prev
        end
    end
    
    @info "   Metropolis-Hastings: Tasa de aceptación = $(round(acc/n_samples * 100, digits=2))%"
    return samples
end

"""
MCMC: Gibbs Sampler para normal bivariada.
"""
function gibbs_sampler(μ, Σ, n_samples::Int)
    samples = zeros(n_samples, 2)
    ρ = Σ[1,2] / (sqrt(Σ[1,1]) * sqrt(Σ[2,2]))
    
    samples[1, :] = μ
    
    for i in 2:n_samples
        # x_2 (current) | x_1 (previous)
        m2 = μ[2] + ρ * (sqrt(Σ[2,2])/sqrt(Σ[1,1])) * (samples[i-1, 1] - μ[1])
        s2 = sqrt(Σ[2,2] * (1 - ρ^2))
        samples[i, 2] = rand(Normal(m2, s2))
        
        # x_1 (new) | x_2 (current)
        m1 = μ[1] + ρ * (sqrt(Σ[1,1])/sqrt(Σ[2,2])) * (samples[i, 2] - μ[2])
        s1 = sqrt(Σ[1,1] * (1 - ρ^2))
        samples[i, 1] = rand(Normal(m1, s1))
    end
    
    return samples
end

using LinearAlgebra

println("\n1. MODELO DE ISING 1D (Solución Exacta)")

function ising_1d_partition(N, J, h, beta)
    """
    Función de partición 1D (boundary conditions periódicas)
    Z = Tr[T^N]
    Donde T es la matriz de transferencia
    """
    # Transfer matrix: T[s,s'] = exp(β(Js·s' + h(s+s')/2))
    T = zeros(2, 2)
    
    # s, s' ∈ {-1, +1} → indexar como {1, 2}
    spins = [-1, 1]
    
    for i in 1:2
        for j in 1:2
            s = spins[i]
            sp = spins[j]
            
            T[i, j] = exp(beta * (J * s * sp + h * (s + sp) / 2))
        end
    end
    
    # Z = Tr(T^N) = λ₁^N + λ₂^N
    eigenvals = eigvals(T)
    
    Z = sum(λ -> λ^N, eigenvals)
    
    return Z, eigenvals
end

function ising_2d_critical_temperature(J)
    """

# Magnetización espontánea (T < T_c)
function spontaneous_magnetization_2d(T, J)
    """
    Magnetización espontánea para T < T_c
    m = [1 - sinh^(-4)(2J/kT)]^(1/8)
    """
    T_c = ising_2d_critical_temperature(J)
    
    if T >= T_c
        return 0.0
    end
    
    x = 2 * J / T
    m = (1 - sinh(x)^(-4))^(1/8)
    
    return m
end

function ising_mc_step!(lattice, J, beta)
    """Un paso de Monte Carlo (Metropolis)"""
    L = size(lattice, 1)
    
    # Pick random spin
    i = rand(1:L)
    j = rand(1:L)
    
    # Calculate energy change
    s = lattice[i, j]
    
    # Neighbors (periodic boundary)
    neighbors_sum = lattice[mod1(i+1, L), j] + 
                   lattice[mod1(i-1, L), j] +
                   lattice[i, mod1(j+1, L)] +
                   lattice[i, mod1(j-1, L)]
    
    dE = 2 * s * J * neighbors_sum
    
    # Metropolis criterion
    if dE < 0 || rand() < exp(-beta * dE)
        lattice[i, j] *= -1
    end
end
